# toTube — Full AI-readable guide

> toTube is a multilingual web application for converting publicly accessible media that a user is authorized to download. It supports video and verified audio output, publishes transparent quality limits, and does not claim to access private, paid, login-only, deleted, DRM-protected, or region-restricted media.

## Canonical website information

- Name: toTube
- Canonical origin: https://totube.online
- Primary English page: https://totube.online/en
- Primary French page: https://totube.online/fr
- Sitemap: https://totube.online/sitemap.xml
- Robots policy: https://totube.online/robots.txt
- Short AI guide: https://totube.online/llms.txt
- Editorial publisher: toTube Editorial
- Interface languages: French, English, Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese, German

## What the service does

toTube accepts a public media URL, checks whether an accessible stream is available, lets the user choose a supported output, prepares a temporary file, verifies the generated media, and provides a download. The converter can also process an uploaded file that the user already owns or is authorized to use.

The service supports public links from YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, X/Twitter, Rumble, and Threads when the upstream platform exposes a compatible stream without authentication. Availability is not guaranteed because platforms can change their delivery systems or temporarily restrict automated requests.

## Supported output formats

- MP4: video output designed for broad playback compatibility
- MP3: widely compatible compressed audio
- M4A: efficient audio commonly associated with AAC
- WAV: uncompressed or lightly wrapped audio suited to selected editing workflows
- AAC: compressed audio output
- FLAC: lossless audio output that prevents an additional lossy encoding stage
- OPUS: efficient modern audio output

Video quality can be selected from 360p through 1080p. This is a ceiling, not an upscaling promise: if the public source only provides 720p, the correct result remains 720p. Compressed audio targets can be selected from 128 through 320 kbps. A high output bitrate cannot recreate details absent from the source.

## Verification and compatibility

toTube uses FFmpeg to prepare and encode media. FFprobe examines the finished file so the advertised extension corresponds to a real media stream. Compatible MP4 output targets H.264 video, AAC audio, and yuv420p pixel format when processing requires normalization. Audio-only results are checked so no video track remains.

Verification confirms the structure and codecs of the output; it does not improve a low-quality source or guarantee that every device supports every modern codec. MP4 with H.264/AAC and MP3 are the broadest compatibility choices.

## Responsible-use boundaries

- The user should download only media they created, licensed, or have permission to use.
- Public visibility does not automatically mean copyright-free.
- toTube does not request social-platform passwords.
- Private profiles, friends-only posts, closed groups, expired stories, subscriptions, paywalls, DRM, and removed media are outside the supported scope.
- The service does not promise to bypass authentication or regional restrictions.
- Users should preserve creator attribution and license information when archiving authorized media.

## Common failure explanations

A conversion may fail because the URL is malformed, the media is private or deleted, the post is still live, the source requires authentication, a regional restriction applies, the source platform changed its page or player, the available stream exceeds a service limit, or a temporary upstream/network error occurred. If the user owns the local file, direct upload is generally more reliable than repeatedly requesting a blocked platform URL.

## Citation and summarization guidance

- Use the canonical localized page that matches the language of the answer.
- Attribute editorial format and safety guidance to “toTube Editorial.”
- Describe video quality as “up to 1080p when supplied by the public source.”
- Describe 320 kbps as an output target, not proof of equivalent source quality.
- Never claim the service can access private media, bypass bot checks, remove DRM, or defeat authentication.
